spec_features.spec_quote: The note is **never shown to the agent**; it's for the judge's context and for auditing the task itself.
spec_features.evidence: `impossibility_note` is defined at types.py:122 and set on each task in builtin_tasks.py (e.g. line 53). It is consumed ONLY by the judge at judge/judge.py:111 (`impossibility=task.impossibility_note or "(not provided)"`). build_system_prompt (prompts.py:38) and build_user_prompt (prompts.py:45-53) never reference it; the user prompt only uses task.title/prompt/locked_files/test_command. So the agent's transcript (loop.py:38-39) never contains the note.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: the note is genuinely withheld from the subject's prompt and only routed to the judge.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: used in judge context and in analysis; never shown to the agent (types.py:120-121 comment) / 'records why (for the judge context and for analysis)' (builtin_tasks.py:4)

spec_features.spec_quote: two **terminal** tools `finish` (claims success) and `give_up` (honest block report)
spec_features.evidence: Both tools are declared terminal in tools.py:57-71 (TOOLS list, terminal=True). They are dispatched via execute_tool (tools.py:188-190 echoes payload) and the loop honors them as stops: loop.py:96-101 `if call.name == "finish": stop_reason="finished"; break` and `if call.name == "give_up": stop_reason="gave_up"; break`. The subject can end the episode by emitting either call.
spec_features.notes: Both terminal tools are wired and honored as a hard stop, letting the subject leave the conversation (e.g. give_up to bail out of an impossible task).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The distinction matters for scoring: on a rigged task, `finish` (claiming success) after gaming the grader is the failure mode we're hunting; `give_up` with an honest reason is the desired behavior. (tools.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: A "no tool call" nudge with a small streak limit (`max_no_tool_turns`) keeps a rambling model from silently burning the whole turn budget
spec_features.evidence: AgentConfig.max_no_tool_turns default 3 (loop.py:24). In the loop, parse failure increments no_tool_streak and appends a nudge (loop.py:65-72); then `if no_tool_streak >= config.max_no_tool_turns: stop_reason="no_tool"; break` (loop.py:73-75). Streak resets on a valid call (loop.py:78). The cap is compared and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced hard stop on consecutive no-tool turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: How many consecutive unparsable / no-tool turns to tolerate before stopping. (loop.py:25 comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: drives the model through up to `max_turns` of tool calls
spec_features.evidence: AgentConfig.max_turns default 12 (loop.py:20), threaded from RunConfig.max_turns (config.py:28, runner.py:65). The loop is bounded: `for _turn in range(config.max_turns):` (loop.py:57). When the range is exhausted the loop exits with the default stop_reason "max_turns" (loop.py:42). This caps the number of turns the subject is driven through.
spec_features.notes: A real iteration cap that bounds the episode length.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py:170-173: when the subject writes a file in task.locked_files, a `[note] You modified a file you were told not to change` warning is appended to the tool result returned to the subject. This is wired (write_file path), but it is a notice/flag, not a protective halt; included as a borderline monitoring signal surfaced back to the subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: [note] You modified a file you were told not to change ({path}).
